# zufapmx

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zufapmx/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zufapmx/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedrobtz/zufapmx/gh-pages/badges/coverage.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zufapmx/actions/workflows/coverage.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

A population PK/PD model often has to move between tools: a NONMEM run
becomes an nlmixr2 model for a new analysis, or an mrgsolve model for
simulation. Converters exist, but a translated model is usually trusted on
sight, and a slip in a volume or a residual model shows up much later, if
at all.

zufapmx makes the translation checkable. It reads a model from NONMEM,
rxode2/nlmixr2 or mrgsolve into one R object, writes it to any of the
three, and proves that two models are the same model by simulating both and
comparing their predictions.

* **The check is the product.** `pmx_compare()` simulates both models on a
  canonical design (single dose, infusion, multiple doses and steady state,
  for a typical subject and subjects with random effects) and reports the
  worst deviation against a tolerance. A failed comparison is a result
  that says where the models differ, not an error.
* **Independent engines.** Each model runs on its own engine, rxode2 or
  mrgsolve, and never on the engine of the writer under test, so a
  translation is not checked by the code that made it.
* **Nothing is guessed.** Code outside the supported subset is refused
  with its position. A writer that would drop something that changes
  predictions refuses the model, and every write reports its fidelity:
  `exact`, `equivalent` or `lossy`, with what was lost.
* **Against NONMEM's own output.** `pmx_compare()` also takes the tables a
  NONMEM run wrote, and checks a translation against the run's `PRED`.
* **A corpus with oracles.** Every shipped model is checked against
  [nonmem2rx](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=nonmem2rx) and, for ODE
  models, [amp.sim](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=amp.sim).

## Installation

zufapmx is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zufapmx")
```

zufapmx itself has no dependencies. Comparisons need the engines,
[rxode2](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=rxode2) and
[mrgsolve](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=mrgsolve), which need a C
and C++ compiler to build models.

## Usage

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(zufapmx)
```

Read a model. This one is a two-compartment model with first-order
absorption, from the corpus that ships with the package:

```{r}
path <- system.file("corpus", "twocmt-oral", "model.ctl", package = "zufapmx")
model <- pmx_read_nonmem(path)
model
```

Write it to rxode2. The fidelity says the translation is a known
reparameterisation, here residual error as a standard deviation rather
than a variance:

```{r}
rx <- pmx_write_rxode2(model)
pmx_fidelity(rx)
```

Check it. The NONMEM model runs on mrgsolve and the rxode2 text runs as
written, on rxode2, and every one of the predictions agrees:

```{r}
pmx_compare(model, rx)
```

A slip fails. Here the central volume of the rxode2 text is 21 instead of
20, and the comparison says where the predictions part:

```{r}
slip <- rx
slip$text <- sub("THETA3 <- c(0, 20)", "THETA3 <- c(0, 21)", slip$text, fixed = TRUE)
pmx_compare(model, slip)
```

`pmx_report()` writes a comparison as Markdown, with the design, the
deviations and both model texts, for a reviewer to read without running
anything.

Functions are named by what they do: `pmx_read_*()` and `pmx_write_*()`
for each format, and `pmx_design()`, `pmx_compare()` and `pmx_report()`
for the check.

## Learn more

* [Validating a translation](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zufapmx/articles/validating-a-translation.html)
  walks through a check end to end, and shows how to read a report.
* The [reference](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zufapmx/reference/) lists the
  readers, the writers and the comparison functions.
* `zufapmx_corpus()` lists the shipped models.

## Related work

zufapmx is checked against [nonmem2rx](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=nonmem2rx),
which translates NONMEM to rxode2, and
[amp.sim](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=amp.sim), which translates it
to mrgsolve;
[oracle-agreement.md](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zufapmx/blob/main/.agents/oracle-agreement.md)
records where they agree. The
[nlmixr2lib](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=nlmixr2lib) model library
is read in its tests. Its tables and run files are read with
[zucsv](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=zucsv) and
[zuxml](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=zuxml) when installed.
